title: Compliance Gate Lifecycle: Handoff, Drift Detection, and Sprint Cadence for SOC2/ISO Delivery
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a repeatable gate lifecycle that ties engineering sprints to compliance artifact handoffs, introduces automated drift detection on evidence sets, and reduces last-mile audit baking. This ticket codifies the gate definitions, handoff responsibilities, required artifact schemas, automation signals for drift, and the sprint cadence that teams must follow when targeting SOC2/ISO deliverables.

Background: Audit cycles have repeatedly hit delays during the final evidence collection week due to unclear ownership, late config changes, and missing logs from private deployments. Current playbooks are fragmented across Confluence pages and ad-hoc slack threads. We need a single orchestrated lifecycle that integrates with Console dashboards and the CD pipeline so teams can plan earlier and avoid scope slips.

Scope and deliverables:
- Gate matrix (Definition Gate/Pre-audit/Assertion/Final sign-off) with explicit artifact lists per gate (config exports, KMS logs, SSO config snapshots, audit-log retention proof, e2e test runs).
- Handoff token concept: a tiny signed artifact (JSON blob) generated by the owning team and attached to the release to prove gate readiness.
- Drift detection rules: automated checks that surface when any artifact deviates from the snapshot attached to the last gate (e.g., SSO endpoints changed, audit policy modified, retention TTL decreased).
- Sprint cadence mapping: recommended scheduling pattern (T-6 weeks: planning; T-4 weeks: artifact freeze; T-2 weeks: automated gating; T-0: reviewer sign-offs).
- Console integrations: per-route compliance checklist widget + a compliance signal feed that can be linked to a PR or release.
- Runbook snippets for on-call and release engineers for last-mile remediation (rollback guidance, compensation plan for missing telemetry).

Non-goals:
- Full SOC2 auditor liaison (this ticket focuses on engineering/product gating, not vendor engagement).
- Deep policy authoring for customers’ legal teams.

Success metrics (OKR-aligned):
- Reduce compliance-related release delays by 60% for customers in pilot.
- Surface 90% of drift events automatically within 10 minutes of change.
- Decrease manual evidence collation time by 70% for targeted flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Gate matrix doc published in Confluence with sign-off from Security and Legal.
- Handoff token spec landed and validated in a prototype for 2 internal teams.
- Drift rule set implemented for SSO config + audit-log retention and linked to a Console alert.
- Sprint cadence guidance published and referenced in two team roadmaps.

2025-03-03 - Engineering sync (Sasha Patel): Proposed drift detection approach: use a lightweight checksum-on-blob and diff against S3 snapshots, plus Console policy hooks. Concerns: false positives for expected fuzz (timestamps). Trade-off: normalize artifacts (strip volatile fields) vs more complex tolerance rules. Decided to normalize first and iterate.
2025-03-04 - Design review (Rafael Ortiz): Shared compliance widget mockups. Need a compact list view for release pages and an expanded timeline for auditors. Will add accessibility checks.

review_feedback: Security: token must include signer identity and expiry; prefer KMS signing instead of app-level HMAC.
Engineering: normalize artifacts to avoid timestamp noise; propose a JSON schema version field.
Design: compliance widget should surface a single actionable button (Recompute Snapshot) for engineers to re-capture current state.
PM: ensure pilot customers are opted in and NDA/consent for evidence snapshots is captured.
